title: Patty Melt Bowls with Caramelized Onion Gravy
description: Soft beef patties carry the flavors of rye and Swiss beneath a ladle of caramelized onion gravy.
equipment: Immersion blender and deep heatproof jug

ingredients.name: soft seedless rye bread
ingredients.note: Remove crust and tear finely; choose a lower-sodium loaf.

ingredients.name: small yellow onion
ingredients.note: Peel and cut into very thin half-moons.

ingredients.name: low-sodium beef broth
ingredients.note: Choose plain meat-and-bone broth without a vegetable blend.

steps.title: Caramelize the onion
steps.text: Cook {onion} in {butter} in the cast iron over medium-low heat for 18–25 minutes. Stir often and use small splashes of {broth} to loosen the pan until the onion is uniformly soft and deep gold.

steps.title: Soften the rye
steps.text: While the onion cooks, mash {rye} with {milk} in a bowl and let stand 4 minutes until no firm pieces remain.

steps.title: Shape thin patties
steps.text: Gently fold {beef} into the softened rye. Shape into two small patties per serving, about 1/2 inch thick.

steps.title: Build the braising gravy
steps.text: Blend the caramelized onion with the remaining {broth} in a deep heatproof jug until smooth. Return to the cast iron and bring to a gentle simmer.

steps.title: Poach the patties
steps.text: Nestle the patties into the shallow gravy and spoon some over them. Cover and cook over medium-low for 7–11 minutes, turning once, until the center of each patty measures 160°F. Keep the patties on a covered plate with a spoonful of gravy.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the freshly stirred slurry into the simmering sauce and stir for 1 minute, until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Melt in the Swiss
steps.text: Take the skillet off the heat and stir in {swiss} until smooth.

steps.title: Serve the bowls
steps.text: Slip the patties back into the gravy. Spoon a pool into each bowl and ladle the rest over the patties.

notes: Make ahead: Caramelize the onions a day ahead and chill. Soak the rye while the gravy warms. For dairy-free bowls use avocado oil for the butter, unsweetened oat milk for the panade and omit the Swiss. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the cooked patties in the onion gravy for up to 2 months; Swiss melts most smoothly if added after reheating. Fridge reheat: Warm a single portion with its sauce in a covered HexClad skillet over medium-low, adding a splash of water if thick. Stir or turn gently and begin checking after 5 minutes. Heat the food to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Use the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 306 kcal, 32.1 g protein, 10.9 g total carbohydrate, 13.8 g fat, 1.1 g fiber, 181 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
